battle.name: 秘魯獨立戰爭
battle.brief: 1809年拉巴斯起義揭開戰端，1824年阿亞庫喬一役決定一切。西班牙王室的野砲沿安第斯山道列陣，以砲火居高臨下封鎖隘口，令缺乏重砲的起義軍屢戰屢敗。蘇克雷卻把野砲拉到平原低地，十二門砲先行展開，砲火壓住高地上的皇家軍砲兵，騎兵趁隙衝鋒，迫使總督德拉塞爾納當日投降。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 交戰一方是西班牙王國及其美洲殖民體系：以利馬為首的秘魯總督轄區是主戰場，玻利維亞總督轄區、聖地牙哥總督轄區與新格拉納達總督轄區同樣被捲入這場戰爭。西班牙方面的指揮系統以總督府為頂端，之下設陸軍參謀總部與各師團，砲兵編為四門一隊的砲兵中隊，每隊由一名上尉率領並配足炮手與騾匹，另有留給圍城與要塞的重砲隊，以及封鎖沿岸港口的海軍分艦隊。另一方是秘魯獨立運動：1809年拉巴斯政變與庫斯科執政會議先後拉起旗號，1810年胡寧科、塔卡納等地起義接連響應，1820年聖馬丁率解放軍渡海登陸，玻利瓦爾自委內瑞拉與新格拉納達揮軍北上，智利與阿根廷的解放軍由南方參與，英國與愛爾蘭的流亡者組成英國兵團受僱於獨立軍，玻利維亞亦有解放軍加入同一陣線。獨立方的組織由執政會議與後來的總統府掌政，軍隊分軍、師、旅三級，各級配屬獨立的砲兵隊與後勤隊，山地作戰仰賴地方村鎮提供的騾匹、牛皮筏與勞役。
countriesEn: One belligerent was the Spanish Crown and its American colonial system: the Viceroyalty of Peru, centred on Lima, was the main theatre, while the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, the Viceroyalty of Chile and the Viceroyalty of New Granada were all pulled into the same war. On the Spanish side the chain of command ran from the viceregal government at the top, through a general staff and the provincial line regiments, with the artillery organised in four-gun batteries called artillery squadrons, each led by a captain and supplied with its gunners and mules; separate heavy batteries were reserved for sieges and fortresses, and a naval squadron blockaded the coastal ports. The other side was the Peruvian independence movement: the 1809 revolt of La Paz and the Cuzco junta raised the banner first, the risings of Huánuco, Tacna and other towns followed in 1810, José de San Martín landed with the Liberating Army in 1820, Simón Bolívar marched in from Venezuela and New Granada, the armies of liberation of Chile and Argentina joined from the south, and British and Irish exiles formed a British Legion in foreign service with the insurgents, while Bolivia's own liberators entered the same ranks. On the insurgent side political authority rested with the juntas and later the presidency, and the forces were organised in army, division and brigade, each with its own artillery and service units, mountain operations depending on the mules, hide rafts and compulsory labour levies that the Andean villages could provide.
people: 關鍵人物橫跨兩大陣營。起義方最著名的領袖是圖帕克·阿馬魯二世，本名何塞·加夫列爾·孔多爾坎基·諾格拉，1780至1781年已在安第斯山東麓率領大規模起義；1809年他被推舉為「印加的後繼者」，同年7月26日在庫斯科被斬首，屍身懸於籠中示眾數月。庫斯科執政會議的領袖、後來秘魯共和國的第一任總統，是何塞·德拉里瓦阿格羅；他於1814年在查帕斯與比爾卡班巴兩役潰敗，1823至1824年在玻利瓦爾進軍下退守山區，1824年死在卡亞俄的囚禁之中。解放軍的樞紐是聖馬丁：他自阿根廷出發，1820年9月在帕拉卡斯登陸，1821年4月於塞羅德帕斯科以砲戰取勝，1821年7月28日在利馬宣布獨立，1824年底辭軍返國。玻利瓦爾在北方打響委內瑞拉與新格拉納達的戰事，並於1823年12月率解放大軍進入秘魯。統率阿亞庫喬的蘇克雷是玻利瓦爾的委內瑞拉同鄉，1824年8月6日於胡寧取勝，12月9日在阿亞庫喬以十二門野砲壓倒皇家軍砲兵。伊西多羅·蘇亞雷斯率死亡驃騎兵在胡寧策動衝鋒；英籍的威廉·米勒是獨立軍砲兵總監；奧伊金斯自智利越過安第斯山，趕上塞羅德帕斯科之戰；英國海軍少將科克倫率智利分艦隊兩度砲擊卡亞俄。西班牙方面的關鍵人物則是總督何塞·德拉塞爾納、參謀長號稱「坎特拉克」的何塞·德拉馬爾，以及何塞·德·拉·佩蘇埃拉；1814年在比爾卡班巴擊潰里瓦阿格羅的，是英籍將軍哈特利。
peopleEn: The decisive figures straddle both camps. The best known leader of the rising was Túpac Amaru II, born José Gabriel Condorcanqui Noguera, who had already led the great insurrection of 1780–81 in the eastern foothills of the Andes; in 1809 he was proclaimed heir to the Incas and was beheaded in Cuzco on 26 July, his body displayed in a cage for months. The Cuzco junta and later the first president of the republic of Peru was José de la Riva-Agüero, defeated in 1814 at Chupas and Vilcabamba, forced into the highlands by Bolívar's invasion in 1823–24, and dead in captivity at Callao in 1824. In the army of liberation San Martín was the hinge: he crossed from Argentina, landed at Paracas in September 1820, won the artillery duel of Cerro de Pasco in April 1821, proclaimed independence in Lima on 28 July 1821, and resigned to return to Europe at the end of 1824. Bolívar fought the war in the north and led his great liberating army into Peru in December 1823. Sucre, Bolívar's Venezuelan compatriot, commanded at Ayacucho; he won at Junín on 6 August 1824 and on 9 December 1824 brought twelve field guns into action against the royalist artillery. Isidoro Suárez led the Húsares de la Muerte in the charge at Junín, Guillermo Miller, a Briton by birth, was the artillery director of the insurgent army, O'Higgins crossed the Andes from Chile in time for Cerro de Pasco, and the British Admiral Cochrane twice shelled Callao with his Chilean squadron. On the Spanish side the key names were the viceroy José de la Serna, the commander-in-chief José de la Mar, known as Canterac, and Joaquín de la Pezuela; the general who destroyed Riva-Agüero's army at Vilcabamba in 1814 was the British-born officer Hartley.
kits: 本卡的野砲出自16世紀西班牙的野戰砲兵制度：1550年前後，阿爾瓦洛斯公爵頒行的軍令把輕野砲按比例配給部隊，每百名步兵配一門八磅或十二磅的野砲，每千步騎兵另設砲隊；砲身可拆成數件分載於馬車，備件與火藥另車隨行，行軍由騾隊牽引。這套制度讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火，也讓砲火用量成為可估算的戰術語言。秘魯獨立戰爭中，西班牙軍仍沿用這套編制：每砲兵中隊四門，炮手六至八人，一門砲連同藥箱約需六匹騾，另有專職的騾夫隊。野砲之外，皇家軍尚有十二磅、十八磅乃至二十四磅的重砲，多留給卡亞俄要塞與圍城使用；進入安第斯山區後，車載砲難以通行山道，遂改用騾馱的山砲與短管迫擊砲，倚靠高地封鎖隘口。獨立軍初年缺乏火藥與砲身，1809年5月6日潘帕·德拉基努亞一役繳獲的皇家軍砲兵場，計約四十門砲與大批火藥，成為起義軍砲兵的底子；1820年聖馬丁由阿根廷運來火藥並新購野砲，交由威廉·米勒整編，構成塞羅德帕斯科與阿亞庫喬兩役的砲兵骨幹。除火器之外，兩軍亦用刺刀長矛、獵槍、馬刀，乘騎多為克里奧爾馬，運輸靠騾與牛車，防守方在卡亞俄還有重砲與從艦上射擊的岸防砲火。
kitsEn: The field gun on this card comes out of the sixteenth-century Spanish system of field artillery: in the ordinances of about 1550 issued under the Duke of Alba, light field pieces were allotted to troops in fixed proportion, one eight- or twelve-pounder to every hundred foot and additional batteries for every thousand men in foot and horse alike; the barrel could be broken down and carried in several pieces on wagons, with spare parts and ammunition on separate vehicles, and the teams were hauled by mules. That system gave field combat, for the first time, artillery fire that could be calculated, and made the expenditure of powder a quantifiable tactical language. In the Peruvian war of independence the Spanish army still used that organisation: four guns to an artillery squadron, six to eight gunners per piece, about six mules needed for each gun with its ammunition, and separate mule-driver teams. Besides the field pieces the royalists had twelve-, eighteen- and even twenty-four-pounder heavy guns, which were mostly kept for the fortress of Callao and for sieges; once they entered the Andes, wagon-borne guns could not pass along the mountain roads, so they fell back on mule-borne mountain guns and short-barrel mortars, holding the passes from the heights. The insurgents at first had neither powder nor barrels: the royalist artillery park captured at Pampa de la Quinua on 6 May 1809, roughly forty guns and a great quantity of ammunition, became the base of the rebel artillery, and in 1820 San Martín brought powder from Argentina and bought new field guns, which Guillermo Miller reorganised into the gun crews that fought at Cerro de Pasco and at Ayacucho. Beyond firearms both armies used bayonets, pikes, shotguns and sabres, rode Creollo horses, and moved supplies by mule and ox cart, while the defenders of Callao added heavy pieces and naval gunfire against the shore.
tactics: 西班牙16世紀的野砲用法，主線是線列陣前的固定砲位：步兵列在前，野砲位於陣前或側翼，齊射後退回陣線後裝填，進攻次序與射速都按條令計算。安第斯山區把這套戰術扭成另一副模樣，地形決定一切，路口、隘口與山脊高地的控制權比兵力更重要，砲兵被迫沿羊腸小道展開，火力難以集中，射界也常被山勢切斷。1813至1814年，皇家軍在查帕斯與比爾卡班巴以山砲封死通往庫斯科的道路，讓缺乏砲兵的里瓦阿格羅無法展開兵力。聖馬丁的解放軍把野砲用得比對手更細：1821年4月6日塞羅德帕斯科之戰，他以砲兵正面迎擊對方高地的砲兵陣，砲火壓制之後由奧伊金斯率領騎兵衝鋒，奪得八門砲；1824年8月6日胡寧之戰，蘇克雷在海拔約三千三百公尺的高原上以騎兵為主，砲兵退居次要位置，待皇家軍騎兵衝入蘇亞雷斯率領的死亡驃騎兵刀鋒之前，隨即潰散。真正的轉折在阿亞庫喬：蘇克雷把十二門野砲列在低地，步兵四縱隊同時展開，兩翼指向皇家軍砲兵所在的高地，砲火一旦打亂高地陣地，皇家軍騎兵失去掩護才崩潰。補給上，雙方都靠騾隊、牛皮筏與山道上的勞役徵發；海上則由科克倫的智利分艦隊封鎖卡亞俄港口，1816年5月2日與1819年5月9日兩次攻擊要塞均告失敗。
tacticsEn: The Spanish sixteenth-century way of using the field gun turned on a fixed battery position in front of the line: the foot stood in front, the field guns were placed ahead of the line or on its flanks, fired in salvo and then withdrew behind the ranks to reload, and both the order of attack and the rate of fire were calculated by ordinance. In the Andes this doctrine was twisted into a different shape, because terrain decided everything: control of the passes, the road junctions and the ridge heights mattered more than numbers, the batteries had to be extended along narrow mule tracks, their fire could hardly be concentrated, and the line of sight was constantly cut by the mountain itself. Between 1813 and 1814 the royalists used mountain guns at Chupas and Vilcabamba to seal the roads to Cuzco, so that Riva-Agüero, who had no artillery of his own, could never deploy. San Martín used his field guns more finely than his opponent did: at Cerro de Pasco on 6 April 1821 he matched his batteries against the enemy batteries on the heights, and once his fire had mastered them O'Higgins led the cavalry charge that took eight guns; at Junín on 6 August 1824 Sucre fought almost entirely with cavalry on a plateau at some 3,300 metres, the artillery taking a secondary part, and the royalist horse broke as it ran into the blades of Suárez's Húsares de la Muerte. The real turning point came at Ayacucho: Sucre deployed his twelve field guns on the low ground, opened four infantry columns at the same time, and turned two of them against the heights where the royalist batteries stood; once the gun fire had disordered that position the royalist cavalry, deprived of cover, came apart. On the logistics side both armies depended on mule teams, hide rafts and labour levies along the mountain roads, while at sea Cochrane's Chilean squadron blockaded the port of Callao, its attacks on the fortress on 2 May 1816 and 9 May 1819 both failing.
data: 可核對的數字並不很多，以下幾項大致可靠：拉巴斯起義爆發於1809年5月10日；同年5月6日潘帕·德拉基努亞一役，起義軍繳獲皇家軍砲兵場，計約四十門砲與大量火藥；1809年7月26日，圖帕克·阿馬魯二世在庫斯科被處決。1814年1月9日查帕斯之戰、6月13日比爾卡班巴之戰，先後瓦解里瓦阿格羅的北軍。海軍方面，1816年5月2日與1819年5月9日科克倫分艦隊兩度攻擊卡亞俄，第二次雖以火船焚毀外圍船隻，仍未能登陸。陸軍方面：聖馬丁於1820年9月13日在帕拉卡斯登陸；1821年4月6日塞羅德帕斯科之戰奪得敵方八門砲；1821年7月28日在利馬宣布獨立，12月8日正式宣告獨立；1824年8月6日胡寧之戰，雙方投入的騎兵合計逾三千，總督德拉塞爾納中傷被俘；12月9日阿亞庫喬之戰，獨立軍約二千五百人、十二門砲，皇家軍約五千人、十八門砲，皇家軍傷亡與被俘合計逾一千，陣亡與被俘的分配各籍說法不一；1825年1月23日，卡亞俄要塞守軍約一千八百人投降。整場戰爭自1809年至1824年，前後十五年，其間跨越的戰役數以百計，傷亡總數史無明文，只能由各役戰報分別推估。殖民地人口的數字同樣爭議頗大，本篇不列。
dataEn: The verifiable numbers are not many, and the following are broadly reliable: the rising in La Paz broke out on 10 May 1809; on 6 May of the same year the insurgents took the royalist artillery park at Pampa de la Quinua, roughly forty guns together with a large quantity of ammunition; on 26 July 1809 Túpac Amaru II was executed in Cuzco. The battle of Chupas on 9 January 1814 and that of Vilcabamba on 13 June broke Riva-Agüero's northern army in turn. At sea Cochrane's squadron attacked Callao on 2 May 1816 and again on 9 May 1819, the second attempt burning the outlying shipping with fireships but still failing to land. On land: San Martín landed at Paracas on 13 September 1820; at Cerro de Pasco on 6 April 1821 he took eight guns from the enemy; on 28 July 1821 independence was proclaimed in Lima and formally declared on 8 December; at Junín on 6 August 1824 the two sides together put more than three thousand cavalry into the field and the viceroy La Serna was wounded and taken; at Ayacucho on 9 December 1824 the insurgents numbered about 2,500 men with twelve guns against some 5,000 royalists with eighteen, the royalist casualties in killed, wounded and captured together exceeding a thousand, the division between those killed and those captured differing from source to source; on 23 January 1825 the garrison of Callao, some 1,800 men, surrendered. The war as a whole ran from 1809 to 1824, fifteen years in all, and crossed a hundred battles; no overall casualty figure survives, and it can only be estimated battle by battle from separate reports. The population of the colony is equally disputed and is deliberately left out here.
cause: 戰爭的起因有遠因，也有近因。遠因是18世紀的啟蒙思想與克里米爾知識分子對宗主國的不滿：秘魯出生的克里奧爾人自認與西班牙本土的克魯斯哥人同源，卻在總督府、議會與教會的職位上被排擠在後；受過教育的克里米爾人多半止於讀書談論，一般士兵與工匠的不平更無處伸訴。制度上的摩擦集中於稅制與貿易壟斷：秘魯總督轄區每年向母國輸送巨額白銀與稅收，本地卻受年限限制，秘魯商船只能經由加的斯貿易，克里米爾商人不得自由進入總督轄區的內陸貿易區，港口貿易則由西班牙商會壟斷。教會與土地分配的不公，加上那句最常被引用的口號——西班牙人壓迫印第安人，克里米爾人壓迫西班牙人——構成起義最直接的怨情。直接引爆的則是1808年西班牙被法國占領、斐迪南七世退位與波旁王朝的崩潰，馬德里無主，克里奧爾人自行成立執政會議；1809年5月10日拉巴斯的槍聲，把政治抗議變成武裝起義；而1809年8月新任總督何塞·德拉塞爾納到任、各地執政會議被解散、殖民地各城歸入嚴格戒備，衝突便由市政革命轉為公開的戰爭。
causeEn: The war had distant as well as immediate causes. In the distance lay Enlightenment ideas and the resentment of Creole intellectuals towards the mother country: Creoles born in Peru considered themselves of the same stock as the peninsular Spaniards, yet were pushed behind the Spaniard for offices in the viceregal government, the cabildos and the Church, and the better-educated Creoles mostly confined themselves to reading and talking, while the grievances of ordinary soldiers and artisans had no outlet at all. The friction in institutions centred on taxation and trade monopolies: the Viceroyalty of Peru sent enormous quantities of silver and tax to the metropolis, while locally the trade of Peruvian shipping was restricted by law, Peruvian vessels could trade only with Cádiz, Creole merchants were not free to enter the interior trading zones of the viceroyalty, and the carrying trade of the ports was monopolised by the mercantile houses of Spain. Grievance at the Church and at the distribution of land, added to the slogan most often quoted in the risings — the Spaniards oppress the Indians, the Creoles oppress the Spaniards — made up the most immediate resentment. What set it off was the occupation of Spain by France in 1808, the abdication of Ferdinand VII and the collapse of the Bourbon dynasty; with no government in Madrid, the Creoles set up juntas of their own, and the gunfire of La Paz on 10 May 1809 turned political protest into armed insurrection. When the new viceroy José de la Serna took office in August 1809, the juntas were dissolved and the colonial cities were put under strict guard, and the conflict passed from municipal revolution into open war.
impact: 戰爭的直接後果是秘魯的獨立與新國家的建制：1821年的秘魯共和國、1824年玻利瓦爾在利馬組成的「大秘魯」體系，經1826年的秘魯與玻利維亞邊界條約及1836年的秘玻聯邦，把安第斯山中部重新劃成一個政治單位。長期後果更為複雜：共和國時期克里奧爾人與土著身分的衝突被寫入憲法與選舉法，成為19世紀秘魯政治的深層裂痕；秘魯南部與玻利維亞之間的界線，以及玻利維亞銀礦的歸屬，1830年代曾直接引發大規模戰爭；玻利瓦爾在1825年把萬卡維利卡汞礦的存貨運往自己的軍隊，暴露新國家的財政窘迫。戰略上，這場戰爭是歐洲軍制在安第斯的一次總實驗，也讓新生的美洲國家看見砲兵與地理如何決定勝負。國際層面上，1820年代的西班牙深陷自由派與保守派的內鬥，無力有效介入美洲；英國於1819年率先承認秘魯獨立，並以貸款與軍事合作換取貿易利益，荷蘭與美國隨後亦相繼承認。獨立後的秘魯靠外債維持軍費，走上以農礦抵押外債的老路，一路通向1870至1879年的戰爭與1914年喪失塔克納。三個世紀的白銀開採、汞礦提煉與港口貿易中心，隨政治獨立而重新分配權力，秘魯不再是帝國的邊陲，而成了面向太平洋的地緣角色。安第斯山被寫成一部軍事編年史，「解放者」的崇拜成為國家認同的主軸，這也是其後多次政變與內戰的文化土壤。
impactEn: The immediate consequence of the war was Peruvian independence and the building of a new state: the republic of Peru of 1821 and the greater Peru assembled by Bolívar in Lima from 1824, and through the 1826 treaty settling the Peruvian–Bolivian frontier and the Peru–Bolivia Confederation of 1836, the central Andes was redrawn as a single political unit. The long-term consequences were more tangled: the conflict between Creole and indigenous status was written into the constitution and the electoral law and became the deep fissure of nineteenth-century Peruvian politics; the southern Peruvian frontier with Bolivia and the ownership of the Bolivian silver mines brought a large war in the 1830s; and in 1825 Bolívar carried off the stock of mercury from Huancavelica to pay his own troops, exposing the fiscal poverty of the new republic. Strategically the war was a grand trial of European military institutions in the Andes, and it taught the new American states how artillery and geography decided battles. On the international stage, Spain, torn by the liberal and conservative civil wars of the 1820s, could not intervene effectively in America; Britain recognised Peruvian independence as early as 1819 and exchanged loans and military cooperation for trade, and the Netherlands and the United States followed. Independent Peru financed its armies with foreign debt and mortgaged its agricultural and mineral wealth to do so, a road that ran straight to the war of 1870–79 and the loss of Tacna in 1914. Three centuries of silver mining, mercury refining and the pivot of the port trade were redistributed by political independence: Peru was no longer an imperial margin but a Pacific geopolitical actor. The Andes was written up as a military chronicle, the cult of the Liberator became the spine of national identity, and that too was the cultural soil of the coups and civil wars that followed.
result: 結果是西班牙在南美大陸的統治瓦解。1824年12月9日阿亞庫喬一役，蘇克雷以十二門野砲的射程與射速壓住高地上的皇家軍砲兵，砲火一被壓制，皇家軍騎兵便失去掩護而被獨立軍騎兵擊潰，總督德拉塞爾納與一批高級將校當日被俘，殘部退入山區；1825年1月23日，卡亞俄要塞在飢餓與孤立中投降，西班牙在南美洲的殖民統治就此終結，秘魯國旗自1821年7月28日起懸於利馬。戰後的清算同樣殘酷：聖馬丁於1824年12月辭去「秘魯守護者」的職位返歐，玻利瓦爾在1824年10月入主利馬，1826年組建大哥倫比亞聯邦，隨後又把玻利維亞與秘魯北部併入同一聯邦，秘魯的國界在二十餘年間被反覆重畫；1825年秘魯設聖馬丁省等行政區，玻利瓦爾取走萬卡維利卡的汞礦，以及戰後軍費無著所引發的多次內戰，構成新國家的頭號難題。戰役層面上，野砲這類可拆可運、射速可計算的火炮，在安第斯山地最終勝過了依賴高地與圍城的老式要塞砲兵；山地地形、騾馱與騎兵衝鋒，決定了新國家的疆界與軍隊的靈魂。
resultEn: The result was the end of Spanish rule on the South American continent. At Ayacucho on 9 December 1824 Sucre used the range and rate of fire of his twelve field guns to master the royalist batteries on the heights; once that fire was broken the royalist cavalry, deprived of cover, was destroyed by the insurgent horse, the viceroy La Serna and a number of senior officers were taken the same day and the remnants fell back into the highlands. On 23 January 1825 the fortress of Callao capitulated to hunger and isolation, and Spanish colonial rule in South America came to an end; the flag of Peru had been raised in Lima since 28 July 1821. The reckoning afterwards was equally harsh: in December 1824 San Martín laid down the office of Protector of Peru and sailed for Europe; Bolívar entered Lima in October 1824, founded the Gran Colombian federation in 1826 and then drew Bolivia and northern Peru into the same union, so that Peru's frontiers were redrawn again and again over more than two decades. The new state's gravest problems were the administrative departments of 1825, the mercury Bolívar carried off from Huancavelica, and the civil wars that followed the collapse of military pay. At the level of battle, the field gun — a piece that could be broken down, moved on wagons and fired at a calculable rate of fire — finally proved itself in the Andean mountains against the old fortress artillery that depended on heights and siege; the mountain terrain, the mule and the cavalry charge fixed both the borders of the new republic and the character of its army.
